memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'Throughout the period of their dedication to the Lord, the Nazirite must not go near a dead body. Even if their own father or mother or brother or sister dies, they must not make themselves ceremonially unclean on account of them, because the symbol of their dedication to God is on their head. Throughout the period of their dedication, they are consecrated to the Lord.' - Num 6:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Nazirite's dedication was so complete that they could not even take part in the burial rituals of their closest family — not father, mother, brother, or sister. This was a costly commitment. It meant that during the vow, their devotion to God took precedence even over deep family duties.

We must understand this rightly. God is not teaching us to be cold toward our families; elsewhere Scripture strongly commands us to honour our parents and care for our own. The point is the seriousness and wholeness of the Nazirite's consecration. Their dedication to God was total, "throughout the period," without exception.

Real commitment to God will sometimes cost us. It may mean choices that others do not understand, or times when following God feels difficult and lonely. Jesus spoke honestly about this. He said that anyone who loves father or mother more than Him is not worthy of Him (Matt 10:37), and He called His followers to take up their cross.

This is not because God wants to compete with our loved ones, but because He must have first place. When He truly holds first place, we actually love our families better, not worse.

Following God wholeheartedly is worth every cost. Whatever you give up for Him is never lost. He honours devotion that holds nothing back.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has following God ever cost you something?
- Does God truly hold first place in your heart?
- How does putting God first help you love others better?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You deserve first place in my heart. Give me the grace for costly commitment, trusting that whatever I give up for You is never wasted. Amen.
